problems.title: OC1
problems.statement: The map in the answersheet represents the sky somewhere in Nepal. The Zenith is at the center of the chart.

parts.statement: Estimate the latitude of the location from where this sky map is captured. [2.5 points]
Label the cardinal points(N,E,S,W) on the map and spot three planets from the Solar System in the sky map.[1x7 = 7 points]
Draw on the map with continuous lines the celestial equator (EQ), the ecliptic (EC), and the local meridian (ME) and label them.[1.5x3 = 4.5 points]
Trace 10 constellations in the sky map and label them with numbers and write the corresponding latin name of the constellations or IAU code in the table below. [1x10 = 10 points]

Identify and mark the 4 brightest stars in the sky map below. Number the star from 1 – the brightest, and continue with the fainter ones till number 4 for the faintest. Fill in the following table the Bayer designation or the official IAU name of the four identified stars. [1.5x4 = 6 points]

Mark (with a small circle) positions of the following objects and label them. [1.5x7 = 10.5 points]

- M42
- M81
- M41
- M31
- $\gamma$ Ori
- $\alpha$ Per
- $\alpha$ Cyg
Estimate the equatorial coordinates of the star Aldebaran ($\alpha$ Tau). [3 points]

problems.title: OC2
problems.statement: In the table given in the answersheet, fill in the numbers of the pictures as per their category.

figures.alt: A 3×3 grid of nine photographs of Solar System bodies on black backgrounds, numbered 1. to 9.: 1 a grey-brown icy moon, 2 a grey heavily cratered sphere with a bright spot, 3 an irregular cratered brownish moon, 4 a bright white icy moon with long grooves, 5 a dark moon densely covered with bright crater spots, 6 a rubble-pile diamond-shaped grey asteroid, 7 a hazy featureless yellow-orange globe, 8 a lumpy blue-and-grey metallic-looking asteroid, 9 a reddish-brown smooth sphere.

figures.caption: O5

figures.caption: O6
